caption: cgroup
description: The cgroup object describes a Linux control group (cgroup), the kernel mechanism that organizes processes into hierarchical groups for resource control and accounting. cgroups are the basis for container and pod isolation, so the cgroup a task belongs to is commonly used to attribute kernel-level (e.g. eBPF/LSM) events to a container or pod.
name: cgroup

name.description: The cgroup name, typically the last path component of path.

path.description: The cgroup filesystem path relative to the cgroup mount, for example /system.slice/docker-1a2b.scope.

uid.description: The kernel-assigned cgroup ID (the cgroup directory's inode number), stable for the lifetime of the cgroup.

version.description: The cgroup hierarchy version, for example 1 or 2.
